lessons.title: Classes
lessons.content: A class bundles state (properties) and behavior (functions) together. Real scenario: a Lesson class with title, content, codeSnippets properties matching your app's data layer.

codeSnippets.code: class Lesson(val id: String, val title: String, val content: String)

lessons.title: Creating Objects (Instances)
lessons.content: You instantiate a class by calling its constructor - no 'new' keyword needed. Real scenario: instantiating a Repository implementation and injecting it into a ViewModel.

codeSnippets.code: val repo = LessonRepositoryImpl(dao, syncManager)

lessons.title: Properties
lessons.content: Properties combine a field with accessors - Kotlin auto-generates default getters/setters. Real scenario: a computed displayName property combining firstName and lastName.

lessons.title: Custom Getters and Setters
lessons.content: Override the default getter/setter to add validation while still using plain field syntax externally. Real scenario: an age property that throws if set to a negative value.

lessons.title: Constructors Overview
lessons.content: Kotlin classes have one primary constructor and optionally multiple secondary ones. Real scenario: a primary constructor for simple models, secondary for classes needing multiple valid creation paths.

codeSnippets.code: class Point(val x: Int, val y: Int)

lessons.title: Primary Constructor
lessons.content: Declared in the class header; val/var-prefixed parameters automatically become properties. Real scenario: a data model where every constructor parameter is also a property, eliminating boilerplate.

codeSnippets.code: class Lesson(val id: String, val title: String, var isBookmarked: Boolean = false)

lessons.title: Secondary Constructors
lessons.content: Declared with 'constructor' inside the class body, must delegate to the primary via this(...). Real scenario: building a class either from raw parameters or from a legacy format.

lessons.title: init Block
lessons.content: init blocks run as part of primary constructor execution, useful for validation logic. Real scenario: validating a discount percentage is between 0 and 100 at construction time.

lessons.title: Inheritance
lessons.content: Classes are final by default - mark 'open' to allow subclassing, a deliberate design favoring explicit API design. Real scenario: an open BaseViewModel providing shared loading-state logic.

lessons.title: Method Overriding
lessons.content: A subclass overrides an open/abstract member using 'override', mandatory in Kotlin unlike Java's optional @Override. Real scenario: overriding equals()/hashCode() on a class used as a Map key.

lessons.title: Polymorphism
lessons.content: A base-typed variable can hold any subtype instance, dispatching to the actual runtime type's implementation. Real scenario: a List<Shape> computing correct area() per shape without manual type-checking.

codeSnippets.code:
val shapes: List<Shape> = listOf(Circle(2.0), Square(3.0))
val total = shapes.sumOf { it.area() }

lessons.title: Abstraction
lessons.content: Abstraction exposes only what's necessary while hiding implementation details, via interfaces/abstract classes. Real scenario: a PaymentProcessor interface hiding whether it's Stripe, PayPal, or a mock.

lessons.title: Encapsulation
lessons.content: Encapsulation restricts direct access to internal state, exposing controlled access instead. Real scenario: a BankAccount where balance has a private setter, only modifiable via deposit()/withdraw().

lessons.title: Visibility Modifiers
lessons.content: public (default), private, protected, and internal control member visibility. Real scenario: marking a Repository implementation internal so only your app module can instantiate it directly.

codeSnippets.code:
internal class LessonRepositoryImpl : LessonRepository
private fun helperFunction() {}

lessons.title: Interfaces
lessons.content: Interfaces define a contract classes must fulfill, and can include default implementations. Real scenario: your LessonRepository interface, letting you swap implementations without touching ViewModels.

lessons.title: Abstract Classes
lessons.content: Can't be instantiated directly, may contain both abstract and concrete members. Real scenario: an abstract BaseSyncWorker providing shared retry logic while subclasses implement performSync().

lessons.title: Nested Classes
lessons.content: A class declared inside another, without a reference to the outer instance. Real scenario: grouping a small Config helper class only relevant inside its containing class.

lessons.title: Inner Classes
lessons.content: Marking a nested class 'inner' gives it implicit access to the enclosing instance. Real scenario: a RecyclerView ViewHolder accessing the outer Adapter's click listener directly.

lessons.title: object Declaration (Singleton)
lessons.content: The object keyword creates a class with exactly one lazily-created, thread-safe instance. Real scenario: a single shared NetworkClient instance used app-wide.

lessons.title: Object Expressions (Anonymous Objects)
lessons.content: Creates a one-off, anonymous instance on the spot, similar to Java's anonymous inner classes. Real scenario: implementing a click listener interface inline for a single button.

lessons.title: Companion Objects
lessons.content: Attaches static-equivalent members to a class, accessed via the class name. Real scenario: a factory function User.create(dto) or constants scoped specifically to their class.
